question: How many times was a Twitter/X post cited as a reference on the english Wikipedia pages for each day of August in the last June 2023 versions of the pages?

history.name: Citation_Expert
history.content: Task setup and plan: We will use the MediaWiki API to fetch the last revision before end-of-June 2023 for each page "August 1" through "August 31" on English Wikipedia. Then, we will parse <ref> tags and citation templates to count references that link to twitter.com or x.com posts (status URLs). Steps: (1) define inclusion criteria; (2) sample-run for a few pages; (3) implement full script with rate-limit handling; (4) aggregate counts and answer.

history.name: Wikipedia_Citation_Expert
history.content:
Inclusion criteria for counting Twitter/X post references:
- References in <ref> tags that include a URL with twitter.com/<user>/status/<id> or x.com/<user>/status/<id>.
- References via citation templates (cite web, cite tweet, etc.) where the url field points to a tweet status URL.
- Archived links that clearly resolve to a specific tweet status URL.
Exclusions:
- User profiles, lists, hashtag pages, or non-status URLs.
- References where the tweet date cannot be determined from template fields or reliable metadata; for this task, we count the citation occurrence if it’s a tweet status URL, but we will group by the day-of-month indicated in the cited post’s date when available. If date missing, we will not count it.
We should extract post dates from template fields (date, access-date if it’s clearly the post date), or from embedded metadata if present.

history.content:
Validation approach:
- Pilot on 3 pages: August 1, August 2, August 4.
- Use API parameters to get the last revision before 2023-06-30T23:59:59Z.
- Parse and count occurrences of twitter.com/x.com status URLs, extract date fields, and ensure date month==August (year-agnostic). If date not resolvable, exclude.
- If rate limited (HTTP 429), use backoff and retry.

TW_REGEX = re.compile(r"https?://(?:twitter\.com|x\.com)/[^/]+/status/\d+", re.I)

    tw_count = 0

            # This pilot does not parse dates yet; we’ll just count occurrences

Updated script with backoff and wikitext parsing:

import requests, time, re
API = "https://en.wikipedia.org/w/api.php"
CUTOFF = "2023-06-30T23:59:59Z"
PAGES = ["August 1", "August 2", "August 4"]
TW_STATUS = re.compile(r"https?://(?:twitter\.com|x\.com)/[^/]+/status/\d+", re.I)
AUG_DATE = re.compile(r"\b(?:August)\s+(\d{1,2})\b", re.I)

results = []
for title in PAGES:
    params = {
        "action": "query",
        "prop": "revisions",
        "titles": title,
        "rvlimit": 1,
        "rvdir": "older",
        "rvstart": CUTOFF,
        "rvprop": "content",
        "format": "json",
        "formatversion": 2
    }
    for attempt in range(3):
        r = requests.get(API, params=params)
        if r.status_code == 429:
            time.sleep(2 ** attempt)
            continue
        break
    if r.status_code == 429:
        results.append({"page": title, "status": "error", "message": "Rate limited after retries"})
        continue
    if r.status_code != 200:
        results.append({"page": title, "status": "error", "message": f"HTTP {r.status_code}"})
        continue
    data = r.json()
    revs = data.get("query", {}).get("pages", [{}])[0].get("revisions", [])
    if not revs:
        results.append({"page": title, "status": "error", "message": "No revisions found"})
        continue
    wikitext = revs[0].get("content", "")
    tw_refs = 0
    for line in wikitext.splitlines():
        if TW_STATUS.search(line):
            # naive date check on same line or adjacent
            snippet = line
            # check preceding line if available
            # (simplified for pilot)
            if AUG_DATE.search(snippet):
                tw_refs += 1
            else:
                # if no explicit August date in snippet, skip
                pass
    results.append({"page": title, "status": "ok", "twitter_citations": tw_refs})

print(results)
